# Data pre-processing

```{r}
#| output: false

# setup R library's and working directories
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)

# Define variables pointing to the relevant directories
dataDir <- "data"
outDir <- "output"
figDir <- "figures"
```

```{r}
# Read csv and store it in the data variable. Ensure separator is (;) and not (,) to match ESS11e04_2 format.
full_data <- read.csv(here::here(dataDir, "ESS11e04_2.csv"), sep = ";")

# Current size of the data-set.
nrow(full_data)
ncol(full_data)

# Select the columns we will need and store it in a new table.
relevant_data <- select(full_data, trust.in.politicians, age, education, household.income, political.interest, vote)

```

Next we prune the rows where the necessary information needed for analysis is not available.
We remove the rows by filtering by the missing value encoding(s) for each columns. 
For trust.in.politicians, household.income and education the values we filter by are: 77,88 and 99.


```{r}
filter_values <- c(77,88,99)

relevant_data <- 
	relevant_data |>
	filter(!(trust.in.politicians %in% filter_values)) |>
	filter(!(household.income %in% filter_values)) |>
	filter(!(education %in% append(filter_values, 55))) # 55 has the value of other which makes comparison of level of education arbitrary, so we added it to the values that need to be filtered from education.

```

For vote and political.interest the values we filter by are: 7,8 and 9.

```{r}
filter_values = c(7,8,9)

relevant_data <- 
	relevant_data|> 
	filter(!(vote %in% filter_values)) |>
	filter(!(political.interest %in% filter_values))

```

Final pruning step, for age the value we filter by is: 999.

```{r}
relevant_data <- filter(relevant_data, age != 999)

# The size of the data set after selection and filtering.
nrow(relevant_data)
ncol(relevant_data)

```
